requirements.evidence: Contract is met: CreateQueue (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:142) trims the name, slugifies the default or explicit slug and creates active queues. UpdateQueue (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:318-326) takes named nullable params, excludes its own id from the slug check (:340) and locks the queue row. SetQueueAccess upserts or revokes, validates strings against the enum (app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:236-249), checks the entity (:208) and logs only when deleted > 0 (:220). QueuePolicy.call denies non-array permissions (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:570). CallNextTicket authorizes after the active check (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:29). Ticket::call follows lock -> inactive -> authorize -> LogicException (app/Models/Ticket.php:468-498). Migration, enum, model and factory are present. Gap: the race-to-ValidationException mapping relies on a hand-rolled isUniqueViolation (app/Actions/Concerns/ValidatesQueueAttributes.php:111-118). It checks SQLSTATE '23000' or the substrings 'UNIQUE'/'Duplicate', which would miss PostgreSQL's 23505 / 'Unique violation' and let a raw QueryException escape.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through app/Actions with authorization inside each action via Gate::forUser(...)->authorize. A single QueuePolicy holds all abilities. #[Fillable] is set on QueueAccess (app/Models/QueueAccess.php:399), the migration has a reversible down() and PHPDoc is updated. docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md and the CHANGELOG 'Added' section are all updated. Deviations: hand-rolled unique-violation detection instead of the framework's UniqueConstraintViolationException (lazy-code 'installed dependency' rung), and the helper is copy-pasted into SetQueueAccess (:285-292) instead of reusing the trait.

security.evidence: Every action authorizes first (CreateQueue.php:144, UpdateQueue.php:325, SetQueueAccess.php:204), so an employee cannot grant themselves access. Both call paths enforce 'call' inside the lock (CallNextTicket.php:29, Ticket.php:492). Permissions are strictly validated (strict in_array, is_string). The membership/queue entity mismatch is rejected. A corrupted grant denies call. Mass assignment is constrained by #[Fillable]. No UI or unescaped output.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/QueueManagementTest.php covers: default and explicit slugs, name validation (empty/blank/256), per-entity slug uniqueness, lifecycle denial for employee/outsider/other-entity owner with nothing written, update combinations, keeping its own slug vs taking another's, deactivation preserving tickets and blocking issue/call, no delete classes, audit grant/revoke with context, no log on an empty revoke, invalid permissions and cross-entity grants, self-grant denial, the call policy including corrupted JSON, CallNextTicket authorization across every CallMode, Ticket::call ordering, and factory entity consistency. Existing CallNextTicket tests were updated to use managerOf rather than weakened. Missing: no test of the DB-unique-index race path (the QueryException -> ValidationException mapping), and no test of the update-time slug length/empty slug.

simplicity.evidence: isUniqueViolation is duplicated verbatim in app/Actions/Concerns/ValidatesQueueAttributes.php:111-118 and app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:285-292. Catching Illuminate\Database\UniqueConstraintViolationException would remove both. The QueueAccessFactory closures (database/factories/QueueAccessFactory.php:616-635) rely on attribute-expansion order, which adds subtlety. The SetQueueAccess fallback update with manual json_encode (:267) re-implements the cast. The rest is direct.

readability.evidence: Small, focused actions with clear names and helpful comments on lock order (Ticket.php:466-467, UpdateQueue.php:332-333). The policy is readable with a private isManager helper. Minor: the factory comment 'The key order matters' signals fragile code; the trait name ValidatesQueueAttributes also hosts DB-error detection.

scope.evidence: All files serve the task: actions, enum, model, policy, factory, migration, docs, changelog and tests. The managerOf helper in tests/Pest.php is needed by the updated CallNextTicket tests. The only edit to an unrelated line is the CallNextTicket comment (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:36), which reflects the new Ticket::call lock behaviour.

issues.explanation: Unique-violation detection only matches SQLSTATE 23000 or the substrings 'UNIQUE'/'Duplicate'. On PostgreSQL (23505, 'Unique violation') the race would surface a raw QueryException, contrary to requirement 2; catching UniqueConstraintViolationException would be correct and simpler.
isUniqueViolation is copy-pasted from the ValidatesQueueAttributes trait instead of being reused.
No test exercises the DB unique-index fallback path (QueryException mapped to ValidationException) in CreateQueue/UpdateQueue or the SetQueueAccess concurrent-upsert fallback.
The fallback update manually json_encodes permissions, bypassing the model's array cast; this duplicates the cast's behaviour.
The factory depends on attribute-expansion key order, which is fragile and needs a comment to explain.

review.summary: The change adds CreateQueue/UpdateQueue/SetQueueAccess actions, a QueuePolicy, the queue_access table, model, enum and factory, and enforces the call ability in both CallNextTicket and Ticket::call in the required order, with thorough tests and updated docs. Authorization and validation are solid. The main weaknesses are a hand-rolled, driver-fragile unique-violation check, copy-pasted into a second class, and an untested race path. These are approvable with small follow-ups.
